tasks.short: Enter approved copy and artwork into layouts for review.

steps.what: Find the current brief, approved copy, artwork and layout plan.
Prepare copy and image files for placement in the design editor.
Place copy and artwork into frames in the design editor.
Correct overflow, awkward crops and spacing in the design editor.
Send the layout proof and version details for review.

tasks.design: A configured {WORKFLOW} links the approved inputs in {DOCS} and prepares placement assets for the design editor in {OTHER}. Linked content and templates handle repeat layouts; the designer resolves custom placement and visual balance. The flow stores a versioned proof in {DOCS} and routes its review.
tasks.previous_blocker: Files arrived separately, copy changed late, and template setup cost more than small individual jobs justified.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing linked-content features handle repeat work. AI-assisted coding can reduce the cost of small file adapters and validation scripts.
tasks.still_hard: Custom compositions, unreliable source files and late copy changes still require intervention.
tasks.human_edge: The designer sees when technically correct placement weakens emphasis, tone or readability.

ambition.what: Template-based event collateral for regional marketing coordinators

tasks.altitude: The week contains less file preparation and repeated placement. The designer can propose which regional requests fit approved templates; budget and publication rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare repeat publication layouts from linked content.
reach.learn: Content mapping, font handling, linked assets and production preflight.

evidence.claim: Locked template regions and spreadsheet-driven variants are available today.
Linked inputs and versioned proof routing can reduce repeated file preparation; savings depend on template coverage.

assumptions: The target includes repeat formats alongside custom layouts.
Approved copy is identified before population; the flow does not silently rewrite it.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured results.
Build ranges cover a small initial template set.
Access and consultation estimates assume no employee monitoring; national rules may require additional consultation.
unknowns: Which design editor and supported import interfaces are available?
What share of layouts reuse stable templates?
Who identifies the authoritative copy and artwork versions?
Which staff-data uses require consultation under applicable national rules?
research_questions: Can linked imports preserve typography, links and special characters?
Which file defects cause the most placement rework?
new_work: Review prepared assets and failed imports.
Maintain template mappings and font dependencies.
Resolve missing inputs and conflicting versions.
Check that proof routing uses the intended reviewers.

tasks.short: Review final layouts and recommend improvements before approval.

steps.what: Locate the current proof, brief and previous review comments.
Check technical specifications using the design editor and PDF preflight tool.
Assess hierarchy, readability, brand fit and message in the proof document.
Discuss recommendations and resolve conflicting feedback with the marketing manager.
Record approval or return the proof for revision.

tasks.design: A configured {WORKFLOW} assembles the current proof and comments from {DOCS}, then invokes technical checks in the preflight tool in {OTHER}. Designers review the exceptions and make visual recommendations. The marketing manager records a version-specific decision in {WORKFLOW}, which routes revisions or marks the proof approved.
tasks.previous_blocker: Technical checks were separate from proof discussions, and approvals often referred to ambiguous attachments.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing preflight profiles and configurable review flows cover much of the coordination without model judgement.
tasks.still_hard: A technically valid layout can still communicate badly. Stakeholders may disagree about audience, tone or acceptable compromise.
tasks.human_edge: The designer explains why a change helps the audience and negotiates a coherent result.
tasks.altitude: Review time shifts toward visual reasoning and stakeholder decisions. The designer can recommend release readiness with clearer evidence; publication approval remains with the marketing manager.

reach.task: Check whether layout changes alter meaning or hide essential copy.
reach.learn: Proof marks, reading order and editorial escalation.

evidence.claim: PDF preflight software checks PDF/X profiles and reports issues; action lists can perform specified fixes.
Visual judgement and feedback negotiation remain human work; technical checks support only part of the review.

assumptions: Print proofs are included; digital formats need different checks.
Technical checks report issues without silently changing approved artwork.
The marketing manager is the publication approver in this typical workflow.
Time shares include the approval handoff and are planning estimates.
Consultation estimates assume approval records are not repurposed for employee monitoring; national rules vary.
unknowns: Which production profiles and digital accessibility requirements apply?
Who can approve which channels and spending levels?
Are proof annotations exportable and tied to immutable versions?
What access and consultation are required for approval records?
research_questions: Which checks produce actionable findings rather than excessive warnings?
How reliably does the review flow prevent approval of an obsolete version?
new_work: Triage technical warnings and document accepted exceptions.
Maintain reviewer roles and approval routing.
Check that revisions invalidate earlier approvals.

tasks.short: Choose composition, image sizes and typography for a clear visual hierarchy.

steps.what: Read the brief, approved copy, brand guide and output specifications.
Try image proportions and text arrangements in the design editor.
Choose type styles, sizes and spacing in the design editor.
Inspect the proof at intended size and adjust hierarchy and readability.
Save layout settings and explain the chosen arrangement for production.

tasks.design: A searchable library in {DOCS} presents approved specifications and links to reusable styles in the design editor in {OTHER}. Configured grids and text styles accelerate exploration, while the designer chooses hierarchy and optical adjustments. A deterministic exporter records selected settings in {DOCS} for production.
tasks.previous_blocker: Brand rules were scattered across documents, while reusable settings and production notes required separate upkeep.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing style and template features provide the foundation. Small exporters and validation scripts are cheaper to build with coding assistance.
tasks.still_hard: Optical balance, reading rhythm and unfamiliar scripts resist fixed rules. A screen preview may conceal print problems.
tasks.human_edge: The designer decides what the audience should notice first and where a deliberate exception improves communication.

ambition.what: Large-print layouts for readers with low vision

tasks.altitude: The designer spends less time rebuilding settings and documenting measurements. They can propose audience-specific layout standards, with approval from the brand owner before adoption.

reach.task: Translate visual hierarchy into responsive page layouts.
reach.learn: Responsive typography, semantic structure and accessibility testing.

evidence.claim: Template tools support locked regions and repeat variants, which can accelerate established layout patterns.
Style reuse and deterministic setting exports can reduce setup while leaving typographic judgement with the designer.

assumptions: Approved fonts, styles and production specifications exist.
The design editor exposes settings through an export or supported interface.
Reusable styles account for some preparation savings within manual typography work.
Screen-based design is the main means; physical proofs are used when required.
Time estimates cover one format family and are not measured savings.
Access estimates assume no new sensitive staff-data processing; national consultation rules still apply.
unknowns: Which formats, scripts and languages must be supported?
Are font licences valid for the intended outputs?
Which audience accessibility needs are currently underserved?
Who approves changes to the shared brand styles?
research_questions: Which layout settings can be exported without losing local overrides?
Which readability checks match the actual viewing and printing conditions?
new_work: Maintain shared styles and specification links.
Review exported settings for missing overrides.
Test unfamiliar languages and accessibility adaptations.
Retire templates that no longer match production requirements.

tasks.short: Create graphics and layouts for product illustrations, logos and websites.

steps.what: Clarify audience, message and creative constraints with the marketing manager.
Explore visual concepts and rough compositions in the design editor.

loop.input: Creative direction, permitted reference assets, brand constraints and requested output dimensions.
loop.output: Up to three rough visual concepts with available generation provenance.
loop.check: Validate files and dimensions mechanically; the designer checks relevance, visual defects, product accuracy and suitability.
loop.stop: Generate three candidates and allow one revision batch; then stop and fall back to manual exploration.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover established formats but cannot supply unfamiliar visual interpretations of an open creative brief.

steps.what: Select and refine artwork in the design editor, checking accuracy and asset rights.
Review the artwork with the marketing manager and agree acceptance or changes.
Export accepted artwork from the design editor and store production files.

tasks.design: A bounded generator in {OTHER} produces rough concepts from a brief in {DOCS}; the designer selects, redraws and refines the result. A configured {WORKFLOW} records acceptance of a specific artwork version before export presets in {OTHER} create production assets in {DOCS}. Available provenance and rights records travel with the assets.
tasks.previous_blocker: Early visual exploration took substantial drawing time, while automated exports did little to help interpret an open brief.
tasks.enabler_now: Image generation offers quick rough candidates, and existing export presets handle repeat production work. Small integrations can now be built more cheaply, without delegating creative acceptance.
tasks.still_hard: Distinctive logos, accurate product details, editable geometry and coherent brand systems still take skilled work. Generated output does not establish ownership or clearance.
tasks.human_edge: The designer creates a defensible visual idea, judges cultural meaning and turns rough material into a coherent identity.

ambition.what: Early visual concept testing with customer panels

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from making every rough option by hand toward developing and testing selected ideas. The designer can recommend which concepts deserve customer testing; brand acceptance and publication rights remain assigned separately.

reach.task: Test whether visual concepts communicate the intended message.
reach.learn: Neutral test prompts, audience sampling and separating preference from comprehension.

reach.task: Prepare graphics for responsive website use.
reach.learn: Asset formats, responsive crops, performance budgets and accessible alternatives.

evidence.claim: Image generation and editing tools can attach machine-readable Content Credentials describing generation provenance.
Prompt-driven editable prototypes can use a team's design system; this supports web exploration rather than proving production readiness.
The digest reports a German court decision denying copyright protection to three generated logos; ownership cannot be assumed.
Rough-concept generation needs human selection, and task-specific savings require a local pilot.

assumptions: Generation is used for rough exploration; logo development still includes substantial human design.
The loop uses an existing generation capability rather than training a model.
Export runs only after acceptance; revision decisions return artwork to refinement.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; relevant disclosure duties must be checked for the intended use.
Provenance records do not establish copyright ownership or permission.
Build ranges assume approved reference assets and an available generation service.
Consultation and access ranges assume no employee monitoring or biometric identification; national rules may extend the schedule.
unknowns: What proportion of work is logos, illustrations or website graphics?
Which reference assets may be processed by the generation service?
What ownership, exclusivity and clearance requirements apply?
Who approves personal-data processing and applicable employee consultation?
Can provenance survive the actual editing and export chain?
research_questions: Does concept generation reduce exploration time after rejection and refinement are counted?
Which product details require manual reconstruction?
Which uses require disclosure under the applicable EU AI Act provisions?
Can accepted concepts be converted into maintainable source artwork?
new_work: Review generated concepts and reject inaccurate or unsuitable material.
Maintain bounded generation instructions and usage budgets.
Record source permissions, generation provenance and human edits.
Maintain export presets and acceptance-version checks.

role.altitude: The designer spends less time preparing files, repeating layouts and chasing proofs, and more time on visual judgement and audience testing. They gain stronger grounds to recommend creative directions and reusable standards; budget, legal clearance and publication authority change only through explicit delegation.
reach: Desktop publishing: linked content, production specifications and preflight.
Market research: comprehension testing of visual concepts.
Web and digital interface design: responsive assets and accessible hierarchy.
Proofreading: copy integrity across layout revisions.
skills_to_grow: Reusable templates, linked content and structured design inputs.
Asset permissions, provenance and disclosure assessment.
Clear creative rationale and stakeholder negotiation.
role.ambitious_version: Lead a visual communication service that tests concepts with audiences, supports regional teams through approved templates, and offers accessible layout adaptations.
